title: Planning and Structured Cognition
position: Core/advanced Mind, Brain and AI pathway
purpose: A core course in the Mind, Brain and AI programme. Search and planning, hierarchical and compositional representations, causal reasoning, structured and program-like hypotheses, analogy and relational reasoning, resource-rational and bounded-rational accounts, generalisation and transfer, and how to tell an observed result from the strategy that produced it.
description: How minds represent structure and solve problems across several steps. Unit 1 is prepared: a model-based planner and a cached policy compared on a grid after three kinds of change, with a laboratory. Units 2 to 8 are outlined; units 6 and 7 wait for verified sources.

outcomes.description: State planning and cached-value strategies precisely enough to compute their behaviour, and predict how each responds to a change in the world.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Hand calculations and laboratory results with saved predictions.

outcomes.description: Name the observation that distinguishes two strategies in a design, or show that none does, and design one that would.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Written analyses of transfer conditions and of the two-step task.

outcomes.description: Keep observed results apart from the strategies and structures proposed to explain them, in reading and in writing.
outcomes.evidenceExpected: Seminar contributions that label each claim and find unsupported steps.

assessmentSpecs.title: Problem sets
assessmentSpecs.description: Hand calculations of planning and learning behaviour on small, fully specified tasks, submitted as immutable attempts with line-localised feedback; revision is expected.
rubricSummary: ties and costs handled as specified

assessmentSpecs.title: Laboratory reports
assessmentSpecs.description: Predictions saved before each run, results with their seeds, the discriminating observation named for each condition, and a stated information contract for any transfer test.
rubricSummary: the discriminating observation, not a convenient average

assessmentSpecs.title: Seminar contributions
assessmentSpecs.description: Short written analyses that separate results from proposed strategies and propose observations that would decide between them.

provenance.authoringMethod: Unit 1 hand-authored on 2026-10-31 from the Sutton and Barto, Daw et al. (2011) and Tolman (1948) records and the course's planning laboratory; every number in the unit was recomputed with the laboratory code at seed 1. Units 2 to 8 are outlines that cite verified sources where they exist.
reviewerNotes: Sutton and Barto's blocking and shortcut mazes compare Dyna-Q with Dyna-Q+; the laboratory's known-map planner against a cached policy is the unit's own construction and is described as such.
Tolman (1948) is reference-only: its public-domain status rests on the host's report of what APA officials told it.
Daw et al. (2011) is cited from the PMC author manuscript and cannot be imported, because PMC forbids automated downloading.
Units 6 and 7 have no verified source yet; causal learning is prepared in COG-201 and is not duplicated.

centralQuestion: How do minds represent structure and solve problems across several steps?
prerequisiteGuidance: Comfort with probability and with the idea of a model that makes predictions. Reinforcement-learning basics help but are introduced where needed; a targeted bridge, not a whole preceding course.
preparationPath: Unit 1 is prepared: planning strategies compared after changes to the world, with a laboratory. Units 2 to 5 and 8 are outlined with verified sources and are prepared in order; units 6 and 7 wait for sources.
plannedActivities: Compare two planning strategies on a controlled task with an explicit state space and test what happens in a transfer condition, explaining which observations distinguish the strategies.
